summary:
VERDICT: pass, no fatal problem. Overall 7.9. Sub-scores: hook 7.5, stakes 8.5, choice null, branch_distinct 9, cliffhanger 8, hinglish 7.5, performability 7.5, length 8, continuity 7.5. File: <repo>/content/series1/episodes/s1b02/script.hi.json.

Tools: this session has only Read, Grep and Glob, so no shell and no Write. Reading and scoring needed nothing more, so I went ahead. Because of that, review-notes.json was not written. An agent with Write should save this round under critic round 1 in <repo>/content/series1/episodes/s1b02/review-notes.json.

Checks I ran, all by Grep and hand arithmetic, none by script:
- JSON: not parsed. Pattern checks found no comma before a closing bracket or brace, no missing comma between lines, no backslash or tab, and no stray quote inside a value. The key counts fit 9 beats and 29 lines, each with id, speaker, text, emotion_tags and target_seconds.
- Ids: every speaker and on_screen id (kiran, aditya, mausi, billu, chhoti, the_boys) and both locations (bedroom, stairwell) exist in the bible.
- Tags: emotion_tags equal the inline tags on all 29 lines, checked by reading every line; the Grep line count is consistent.
- Timing: spoken 102.6 s, plus 18 speaker changes x 0.3 = 5.4 s, plus silences 16.8 s, equals 124.8 s, which is target_total_seconds.
- Lines and density: 29 lines. About 829 dialogue characters without tags, by hand count, under D-007's 1,050. Average about 8.1 characters a second; the highest line is about 8.9 (l19), and none is over 12.
- Kiran is on screen in 7 of 9 beats.
- यह/वह: the only hit is the rule text in writer_notes.
- No frame holds more than two sheet faces, the boys never show a face, and no set-up runs past 8 s on its targets.
- The hi/en id check could not be run because script.en.json does not exist yet (S5's step).

What works:
- The episode is a different story from s1a02.
- It follows the bible beats and the binding D-007 directions: 8 (Billu says 'बारह' against 'बाईस तोला'), 9 (the boys' hands tighten, 'पी लो। नहीं तो ये पिला देंगे।', then the unheard whisper), 16, 17 and 18.
- The reveal in l26 and l27 lands hard ('अब जाएगी कहाँ? अपने हाथ से पिलाया है तूने।').
- The last spoken line, l29, does not answer the ending question.
- It opens inside s1b01's last image, and s1b03 opens inside its last image.

Why the hook scores 7.5: the first 5 s are the palm insert carried over from s1b01 and a practical stalling line. That works for path-B viewers and is weak for anyone coming in cold. No change is required.

Length (estimate, not measured): the series casting takes in <repo>/content/series1/casting/manifest.jsonl run at about 9.6 to 13 characters a second for Kiran, Mausi, Aditya and Billu, and about 6.5 to 9 for Chhoti's giggled lines. The proof's v4 takes ran 5 to 108 per cent over their targets (30 per cent over in total), but those targets were set near 10 characters a second; this script's average 8.1. I project about 85 to 110 s spoken and about 107 to 132 s of running time. That is inside the 135 ceiling and the 100 to 150 fatal band. The risk is the cut running short, not long. Mausi's coldest lines (l26, l27) may also come out faster than her voice note wants; that is for the voice director to correct.

Must-fix: two items, both cheap. In b9, place Mausi's and Billu's eyes so neither can see Aditya's eye open; the ending question depends on it. In l08, drop to one tag so the binding figure 'बारह' is heard cleanly.

Not verified: that the eye-slit still and silhouette-only boys work in a frame; whether the voices obey any tag; the real cut length.
